prompt: Design a regulated Azure order platform that survives a zone failure, handles ten-times bursts, protects data, restores within objectives and remains operable by a small team.
directAnswer: Define order semantics, idempotency, user SLIs, demand, data class, RPO and RTO. Use management groups and workload-oriented subscriptions with separated production/platform boundaries, Entra groups for humans, managed or federated workload identity, narrow RBAC, Policy and protected audit evidence. Trace DNS and the chosen global/regional frontend through VNet controls to zone-spread compute and private data. Select VMSS, AKS, managed app runtime or Functions from workload and team constraints. Bind immutable artifacts to reviewed IaC plans with progressive rollout and rollback. Size peak plus zone-loss capacity across quota, SKU alternatives, subnet IPs, queue drain, SQL connections and dependencies. Choose Storage/SQL redundancy deliberately, protect keys in Key Vault, retain isolated recovery points and test restore plus business correctness against RPO/RTO. Correlate user SLIs with Azure Monitor evidence and model compute, storage, data transfer, networking, telemetry and recovery cost units.
foundation: Reliable Azure design carries a user operation across scope, identity, path, compute, data, capacity, observability, recovery and cost.
seniorAnswer: I do not count replicas, zone redundancy or backup configuration as proof until surviving capacity, client behavior, restore and the user transaction are exercised.
weakAnswer: Use Front Door, AKS, zone-redundant SQL, geo-redundant Storage and Monitor because Azure manages availability.
whyWeak: It omits semantics, authorization, responsibility, capacity math, retry safety, restore, team burden and cost.
